title.narrative: Policies and programmes on sustainable enterprises, improved productivity and working conditions in SMEs, green jobs and cooperatives are developed and implemented

description.narrative: Türkiye adopted the Human Rights Action Plan in March 2021. Within the Human Rights Action Plan, Ministry of Labour and Social Security was assigned to develop Business and Human Rights Action Plan for Türkiye. MoLSS, in consultation with the social partners and relevant public institutions developed and published “Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights”, where a direct reference is made to FPRW. ILO Office for Türkiye provided extensive technical support to the Ministry in development of the Guiding Principles. The Guiding Principles are laid out under 11 Articles related to business actions on human rights, discrimination, child labour, forced labour, collective bargaining and freedom of association, occupational health and safety, green growth, decent work, guidance and complaint mechanisms. As well as a particular focus has been given to RBC in the Road Map on Alliance 8.7 under the “Duty of Care in Supply Chains” section. ILO will continue to support the constituents on the adaptation to EU Directive on Due Diligence. ILO On the other hand, will continue working with its constituents in the context of inclusive and sustainable business development, social and solidarity economy, green job creation.
